articles.title_zh: Galaxy S27 Release Date: Samsung Bets Big On New 'Pro' Phone
articles.content_orig:
SammyGuru is reader-supported. We have affiliate and sponsored partnerships, so we may earn a commission when you buy through links on our site, at no extra cost to you. Posts may contain sponsored or affiliate link placements. Learn more .
The Galaxy S27 series is rumored to bring a shakeup to the otherwise stale flagship lineup. Alongside the usual base, Plus and Ultra models, Samsung is adding a new, smaller device: the Galaxy S27 Pro . There’s been speculation about which cameras this new Pro will get, along with some hope that Samsung may finally freshen up its lineup.
Already sold on the Galaxy S27? Then don’t preorder without us: our Galaxy S27 Mystery Box includes a premium case, 65W GaN charger, tempered glass screen protector, desktop stand, USB-C earbuds, cleaning kit and two bonus mystery items, and US members who buy through our links at launch can claim one. Leave your number and we’ll text you the moment it opens.
Well, we’ve obtained information detailing the camera sensors Samsung is evaluating for all four phones. Our findings also corroborate earlier reports about the upcoming lineup, although there’s some bad news for those holding their breath for major camera upgrades.
Smartwatch of your choice, up to $499
Let’s start with the two lower flagships. These reuse the exact same camera setup we’re all used to: a 50MP main camera using either a Sony IMX955 sensor or a Samsung S5KGNG sensor. The latter is the exact same sensor found in the Galaxy S26 (review) and Galaxy S26+ (review) . It’s not clear which one they’ll use, or if they’ll mix and match them, but Samsung has at least tested the two, according to GalaxyClub .
The ultrawide lens will use a 12MP Sony IMX564 sensor, which has been in use since the Galaxy S23, while the 3x telephoto will use a Samsung S5K3K1. The front selfie camera will use either a Samsung S5K3LU or a Sony IMX874.
Safe to say, not much is changing, apart from the potential move away from Samsung ISOCELL sensors. If you were hoping for a major camera upgrade, don’t hold your breath.
Here’s where things get a little more interesting, though these two devices will share most of their camera hardware. At least Samsung isn’t keeping all the good stuff locked away on its most expensive phone.
Both will share the same 200MP main camera, using the Samsung S5KHP6 sensor. As tipster Ice Universe confirmed earlier, it will use the updated HP6 architecture. It outputs a whopping 16,320 x 12,240 pixels.
The 50MP ultrawide on both models will use either the Samsung S5KJN3 or the Sony IMX855. Both will also share the same 16MP selfie camera too, which will use a Samsung S5K2P5, a seemingly unannounced successor to the S5K2P2.
The main differentiator comes with the telephoto camera. The Ultra will get a single 5x telephoto lens, rocking either the Sony IMX855 or the Samsung S5KJN3 (yes, the ultrawide sensor used on both phones). The Pro, on the other hand, will have a single 3x telephoto lens, using the Samsung S5K3LD, the same sensor as the Galaxy S26 Ultra’s 3x telephoto. So, while the Ultra gets the longer reach, the Pro isn’t exactly being left out in the cold.
Phew, that was a lot of sensor names. To sum it all up, things won’t be changing dramatically. Samsung seems to be shuffling things around rather than reinventing the wheel. The Ultra could lose its dedicated 3x telephoto camera, while the Pro gets one of its own. That would leave all four S27 phones with three rear cameras.
Josh is a British writer that jumps into the fine details. His background in design shines a light on Samsung hardware, software and the broader ecosystem. His prominence on Twitter/X has helped shape his casual approach, explaining topics in a relatable, down to earth manner. When he's not writing, he's an avid gamer, car enthusiast, UI designer, AI experimenter... He's a man of many talents.

articles.title_orig: China has ‘normalized’ naval presence near Japan since political spat of 2025
articles.title_zh: China has ‘normalized’ naval presence near Japan since political spat of 2025
articles.content_orig:
NEW TAIPEI CITY, Taiwan — In early November, Taiwan’s National Security Council secretary-general tracked more than 100 Chinese military-linked vessels near his island.
But given its scale, the massive flotilla that included coast guard vessels alongside navy warships may have had Taiwan’s maritime neighbor Japan in its sights, military experts say.
They say China has sent an outsized number of its far-seas naval deployments to near Japan’s southernmost islands and nearby waters since a political dispute that erupted in November 2025 over a remark by Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi.
Takaichi told a Japanese House of Representatives committee session that month that a Chinese naval blockade or armed conflict involving Taiwan could constitute a “survival-threatening situation” for her own country not far away. China claims self-ruled Taiwan as its own and has not ruled out the use of force to take it.
“There is a direct link between Takaichi’s statement and the quality and quantity of deployments,” said Stephen Nagy, a visiting fellow with the Japan Institute for International Affairs think tank in Tokyo. “(China) is also sending a signal to Tokyo that if it continues its current position vis-a-vis Taiwan that Beijing will continue these activities.”
China is using the deployments, including live-fire drills, uncrewed drone missions and voyages by entire aircraft carrier groups, to exert an unrelenting, long-term pressure on Japan without violating international maritime laws, analysts said.
“By repeatedly transiting waters around the (southwestern) Islands, China is gradually normalizing PLA Navy activity within the first island chain, expanding its operational experience and creating a pattern of accepted presence,” said Katsuya Yamamoto, director of the Tokyo-based Sasakawa Peace Foundation’s strategy and deterrence program.
The first island chain includes Japan, Taiwan and the Philippines.
“In other words, it is establishing facts on the ground, or rather at sea, that broaden its future freedom of action,” Yamamoto said.
In the seven weeks after Takaichi’s comment, the U.S. think tank Center for Strategic and International Studies logged a spike in “notable” PLA escalatory moves. Over 2025 overall, it said, China showed just a “slight increase” in the number of PLA naval vessels reported operating in waters around Japan, including an increase in the number of Chinese ships within the contiguous zone of the disputed Senkaku Islands, which China calls the Diaoyu.
Deployments near the uninhabited, Japanese-controlled Senkakus have “remained at very high levels” over the past year as before, while joint Sino-Russian missions around Japan and Chinese naval activity near the outlying Japanese islets around the Miyako Island “seem to have increased”, said Jeffrey Kingston, a professor specializing in Asian studies and history at Temple University, Japan Campus.
Chinese and Russian aircraft patrolled in June over the Sea of Japan, followed by a joint naval passage in July in the Miyako Strait near outlying Japanese islets. Chinese and Russian surveillance aircraft did five separate flights near Japan in October.
Spokespeople for the Chinese ministries of foreign affairs and national defense have called China’s military actions fair, valid and peaceful.
China is probably using military moves as one in a series of measures – some economic – to get back at Takaichi for her November 2025 remarks, Kingston said. “They haven’t forgotten, that’s for sure,” he said. “They are in various ways trying to put the screws on her.”
Officials in Beijing still want a retraction of the prime minister’s November 2025 comments but it’s unlikely, Kingston believes.
The Japanese government has verbally protested against Chinese military moves, tracked Chinese ships with its own, and scrambled fighter jets.
Tokyo is now considering a 70 trillion to 80 trillion yen (as high as $508 billion) defense spending plan for the five-year period beginning in April 2027, up from 43 trillion yen in the previous half-decade span, Japanese media outlets have reported.
“As the security environment becomes increasingly severe, cooperation with the ally and like-minded countries is indispensable to peace and stability in the region,” Japan’s Ministry of Defense said in an Oct. 29 statement after a meeting with defense officials from Australia, the Philippines and the United States.
The ministry, it said, “will continue to take advantage of various opportunities to further strengthen such cooperation.”

articles.title_orig: Permitting Bill Would Charge Data Centers Billions for Power
articles.title_zh: Permitting Bill Would Charge Data Centers Billions for Power
articles.content_orig:
Weeks after voters lashed out at data centers in the midterms, Congress is debating a sweeping overhaul of federal permitting rules that could help tech companies more quickly build the facilities.
The bill would speed up federal environmental reviews of a variety of energy projects, including transmission lines and gas pipelines, making it easier for developers to get the power they need to run data centers.
But that help comes with a huge catch: Data centers would also have to pay much more for their electricity under a provision in the bill that would charge the facilities extra for access to the electric grid. That measure would upend decades of federal power rules and potentially save billions of dollars over the next decade for households and other ratepayers.
The push to impose higher costs on data centers underscores how thorny the politics around A.I. have become in Washington. Massive, energy-hungry data centers are spreading rapidly across the country, straining electrical networks and triggering anger in many communities . Voters this month approved at least 40 local ballot initiatives to restrict the facilities.
Some environmentalists who oppose the permitting bill have cast it as a boon to tech companies, arguing that the legislation could accelerate the development of data centers powered by natural gas. The bill would pare back federal environmental laws to speed construction of many types of projects, including gas pipelines, wind and solar projects, high-voltage transmission lines, roads, public transit and housing.

articles.title_orig: To Stop Iran’s Rearmament, Trump Must Confront Russia and China
articles.title_zh: To Stop Iran’s Rearmament, Trump Must Confront Russia and China
articles.content_orig:
Click here to download the JINSA Insight
At the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in Shenzhen, China, on November 18–19, President Donald Trump expects to meet with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin on the summit’s sidelines to discuss getting their assistance in ending the war in Iran, while their two countries are helping sustain Tehran’s war effort. Yet, while the Trump administration has intensified military and economic pressure on Iran, it has simultaneously granted sanctions relief to Russia and refrained from targeting major Chinese financial institutions facilitating Iran’s illicit oil trade.
This contradictory approach risks leaving intact the foreign networks that could finance and rebuild Iran’s postwar rearmament in the event of an accord, as Chinese supplies helped Iran rebuild after the June 2025 12-Day War. Washington must confront the countries enabling Iran’s military recovery, and Shenzhen offers the perfect setting to do so.
Pressure on Iran, Relief for Its Backers
Since the United States and Israel launched Operations Epic Fury and Roaring Lion against Iran on February 28, the Trump administration has executed successive campaigns against Tehran’s revenue streams, procurement networks, and smuggling routes. The U.S. naval blockade, first implemented on April 13 and reimposed on July 14, has prevented, according to U.S. Central Command (CENTCOM), Iran from earning more than $25 billion in crude oil revenue. The Treasury Department’s Operation Economic Fury , launched in April, targeted the financing infrastructure providing the basis for Iran’s trade and shadow-banking networks. In August, Operation Economic Outcast , or Economic “D-Day,” extended pressure on Tehran’s foreign financial enablers through sanctions and warning of secondary sanctions measures. The most recent initiative, CENTCOM’s Task Force Iron Gate , coordinates efforts against illicit shipments and revenue flows across Iran’s land borders and the Caspian Sea, routes the regime has increasingly utilized because of the U.S. blockade.
Despite these initiatives to go after Iran, Washington has pursued competing policies toward the Islamic Republic’s two primary foreign backers. The administration first provided sanctions waivers on Russian seaborne oil in March, a waiver which it extended twice, allowing Moscow to continue earning revenue from sanctioned oil shipments until the relief ultimately expired in June. In October, the administration authorized temporary transactions for Russian diesel until April 2027 and waived multiple provisions included in the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026. The White House justified the Graham Act waivers by saying enforcing the sanctions provisions “would impede ongoing US efforts to negotiate a durable and comprehensive peace agreement between Ukraine and Russia.”
Washington has equally shied away from imposing its most consequential financial penalties on China. While the Treasury has imposed sanctions on China’s independent “teapot” oil refineries, Hong Kong-based intermediaries , and procurement companies enabling Iranian trade, it has stopped short of targeting the broader Chinese financial networks that facilitate Iranian oil payments and move the proceeds into the international financial system. When Xi visited Trump in September at the White House, the two extended their trade truce but reached no agreement on Chinese support for Tehran. The administration appears, therefore, reluctant to make any move jeopardizing U.S.-China economic relations even as it attempts to sever Iran’s foreign financial lifelines.
Russia’s Role in Arming Iran
Russia serves as one of Iran’s most consequential military and intelligence suppliers, helping Tehran lead operations against U.S. forces and regional partners. Since March, Moscow has, according to open-source reporting, provided upgraded Geran-2 attack drones , explosives , satellite imagery , and targeting intelligence that bolstered Iranian capabilities during the war. Reports also indicate that Russia is assisting Iran in developing advanced cruise missiles , which would strengthen Tehran’s ability to penetrate regional air defenses. Russia is equally aiding Iran’s strategy of using its proxy network to open a two-front war, as Moscow is reportedly sharing intelligence with the Houthis to carry out attacks on Red Sea shipping.
Russia’s assistance could become even more consequential after a cessation of hostilities. According to The Telegraph , Iran’s Supreme National Security Council Secretary, Mohsen Rezaei, delivered a November 5 letter from Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei requesting Russian S-400 air defense systems. Tehran has also pursued Russia’s 4.5-generation Su-35 fighters and will reportedly receive them following the war’s conclusion . A prewar Iranian parliamentary memorandum also obtained by The Telegraph outlined plans to deepen cooperation with Moscow on missiles, drones, and air defenses, suggesting that Tehran views foreign military assistance, especially that from Russia, as a central pillar of its long-term survival. Of course, Russia’s war in Ukraine limits what weaponry it can spare to its Iranian partner, but even selective transfers of air defense components and drone technology would raise the cost of future U.S. or Israeli strikes on Iran’s nuclear and missile facilities.
China’s Role in Financing Iran’s Recovery
China has been more cautious than Russia about transferring complete weapons systems during the ongoing war, but it has played perhaps the largest role in financing Iran’s reconstruction through oil purchases and providing critical components for weapons systems to operate. According to prewar statistics, Beijing bought about 90 percent of Iran’s crude oil exports through independent teapot refineries, making it responsible for an estimated 45 percent of Iran’s total government budget. Iran’s reliance on China has continued during the war, with Kpler data identifying Beijing as the only purchaser of Iranian crude in October. On the weapons front, Chinese firms have supplied Iran with the crucial missile propellant precursor sodium perchlorate , as well as dual-use drone components . The full extent of direct Chinese military assistance during the current war remains uncertain, but the presence of these procurement networks could again accelerate Tehran’s rearmament should hostilities end.
Iran is reportedly constructing more durable infrastructure in China aimed at circumventing U.S. sanctions. According to a recent Iran International report , citing a leaked letter from Iran’s Oil Ministry, Iran now controls a terminal in the Ningbo-Zhoushan free trade zone, holds stakes in docks in Shandong province, and owns seven storage tanks in Dalian, Huizhou, Dongying, Weifang, and Zhoushan. This infrastructure allows tankers in the fleet of Hossein Shamkhani, son of the late Khamenei adviser Ali Shamkhani, 51 of whose vessels the Treasury has sanctioned, to unload near refinery pipelines and allows Iran to store its crude in China before securing buyers, which mitigates the impact of existing Treasury designations and suggests that Iran is building sanctions-resistant oil facilities in China with Beijing’s tacit approval or acquiescence.
The Precedent of the 12-Day War
Iran’s recovery in the wake of previous U.S. and Israeli air campaigns against it is a case in point as to why battlefield success alone cannot guarantee lasting strategic gains. Israel’s October 2024 strikes on Iran reportedly decreased Tehran’s capacity to produce solid fuel for ballistic missiles by approximately 93 percent, from enough for 14 missiles per week to just one. Eight months later, operations during the 12-Day War destroyed additional missile production facilities, launchers, and stockpiles, again reducing Iran’s operational arsenal. articles.title_orig: Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh stresses importance of AI to economy, but says it could ‘disappoint’
articles.title_zh: Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh stresses importance of AI to economy, but says it could ‘disappoint’
articles.content_orig:
[The stream is slated to start at noon ET.  Please refresh the page if you do not see a player above.]
Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh on Monday highlighted the potential economic benefits of artificial intelligence while warning that the emerging technology also could lead to widespread job losses or fail to deliver on its lofty expectations.
Speaking in San Francisco before a blue-ribbon task force he assembled to examine productivity and employment, the central bank leader stressed that AI "will have significant impact on the economy, with important implications for monetary policy down the road."
"I stress that while I'm not here to offer predictions, I'm not exactly impartial about American leadership in a time so filled with both challenge and possibility," he said in prepared remarks before his productivity and jobs task force.
In his remarks, Warsh used the term "super intelligence" instead of artificial intelligence and described it as "an entirely new force in economic life and society" that has already begun to transform economic activity. President Donald Trump recently ordered that the U.S. government now use the term "super intelligence" almost exclusively instead of AI.
Since taking the Fed chair position, Warsh has emphasized the importance of AI and its potential to improve productivity and ultimately to be a disinflationary force on the economy.
In his remarks Monday,  he noted that AI could lead to productivity gains that could accelerate real economic growth beyond its current range while keeping employment near full capacity. On the downside, he said "less positive" outcomes include job displacement through automation that could raise unemployment.
At the same time, he outlined a third scenario where AI could simply "disappoint."
"After significant capital investment and stock market gains, expected returns could turn down and equity valuations could fall, leading to an economic slowdown and a more notable rise in unemployment," he said. "In time, the economy would recover, but without the productivity gains."
The potential for AI advancement has driven stock market valuations higher and led to companies raising capital to continue competing.
Monday's conference features discussion panels with business leaders, economists and academics. The final session will be a fireside chat that will include Warsh and task force leader and AI advocate Marc Andreessen, co-founder of Andreessen Horowitz.
Warsh created four other task forces addressing topics such as Fed communication, data reliance, balance sheet policy and inflation frameworks.
The chairman noted that this was the first visit he has made to a regional bank.

articles.title_orig: Gemini rolling out 66 new regional voices on Android and iOS, including 10+ UK dialects
articles.title_zh: Gemini rolling out 66 new regional voices on Android and iOS, including 10+ UK dialects
articles.content_orig:
Following a preview at Google I/O , Google is rolling out 66 new regional voices to the Gemini app on both Android and iOS today. The expansion introduces tailored voice options across U.S. English, U.K. English, Indian English, Hindi, Brazilian Portuguese, Indonesian, and Korean.
For users in the UK, the update brings over 10 distinct English voice options covering a wide range of regional cadences. The lineup includes Geordie, Scouse, Brummie, Scottish, Welsh, Northern Irish, Modern RP, and Multicultural London English (MLE).
This might help reduce the issues that sometimes still occur when English accents , in particular, morph into a hybrid of Australian or even American that has been going on for a while with Gemini Live. We have not yet been able to test to confirm this has been resolved with the update. As someone with a regional English accent, this extra representation with Gemini voices is quite welcome.
According to Google, these voices are tuned for natural pronunciation, pitch, and everyday local rhythm rather than exaggerated stereotypes. Because the focus is on cadence over slang, Gemini will sound like a local without filling its text responses with forced street slang. Once selected, your chosen voice carries across the entire app, applying to both Gemini Live conversations and standard text-to-speech playback when tapping the “Listen” icon on chat responses.
You can preview and select the new options today by tapping the three-dot menu inside Gemini Live, or by heading into the Gemini app settings and selecting “Gemini’s voice.” It’s worth noting that the voices aren’t explicitly labeled by city or region in the app menu, and Gemini isn’t programmed to self-identify which accent it is using if you ask it directly.
Instead, Google notes that locally rooted prompts about food, culture, or sport, such as asking for the best pub in Sheffield for a Sunday roast – my suggestion is not a pub; it’s Turnip & Thyme on Eccleshall Road, FWIW. Or another suggestion from big G is where to find proper ingredients for a traditional Scouse stew; the company says these will naturally bring out the warmth and rhythm of the new dialects.
I’d suggest trying to ask where to get the best pattie and chips in Hull or where to get the best pint in Leeds (it’s Whitelocks).

articles.title_orig: The Nvidia scandal fuels tougher China chip rules as Commerce targets Singapore and Malaysia
articles.title_zh: The Nvidia scandal fuels tougher China chip rules as Commerce targets Singapore and Malaysia
articles.content_orig:
The Commerce Department announced Monday it is cracking down on a loophole that has allowed Chinese firms to skirt export controls on American AI chips.
It marks the first government response since Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned from his multitrillion-dollar chipmaker after admitting to an affair with an alleged Chinese spy — and as romances with at least two Nvidia employees surfaced.
The department’s Bureau of Industry and Security issued an interim final rule that seeks to close a loophole that Chinese firms have used to lease Nvidia’s advanced computing power by going through data centers in third countries, according to a Monday press release .
It was “written by and at the direction of the Department of Treasury and the National Security Council,” according to the release.
It came after Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent criticized the Commerce Department for not acting sooner against Megaspeed — an Nvidia customer for whom Huang lover Alice Huang, no relation, worked –which has been accused of illegally diverting sensitive AI chips to China.
A license will now “be required to export, reexport, or transfer (in-country) advanced semiconductors to Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, or Brazil (and any additional country designated by the Secretary of Commerce, in consultation with the Secretary of State or the Assistant to the President for National Security Affairs) – countries which present a higher-than-normal risk of diversion,” according to the new rule .
Secretary of State Marco Rubio warned President Trump about the former Nvidia boss’ romance with Alice Huang last spring, according to reports. Last week, Jensen Huang resigned following bombshell revelations about that relationship and an affair with senior Nvidia exec Kimberly Powell.
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent on Sunday blamed Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick’s team for the Chinese spy mess, saying the Treasury, State Department, Defense Department and US Trade Representative had been trying “for months” to blacklist Megaspeed.
In a Sunday letter addressed to Lutnick, Sen. Maria Cantwell of Washington – the top Dem on the Senate commerce committee – urged the commerce secretary to reinforce export controls on the sale of AI chips to China.
Chinese firms like Alibaba and ByteDance have “used overseas data centers equipped with advanced Nvidia chips to train advanced AI models,” she wrote. “These companies are exploiting a loophole in US export controls by using advanced American chips in foreign data centers even when those chips are restricted from the [People’s Republic of China].
“Despite warnings from the Bureau of Industry and Security that certain arrangements may violate existing restrictions, the Department of Commerce failed to close this loophole, allowing PRC companies to advance their AI capabilities using sensitive American technology.”
Asked about reports that Rubio had briefed Trump on the alleged Chinese spy plot targeting Huang, the president said Monday, “I haven’t heard that.”
“I don’t know that she [Alice Huang] is a spy,” the commander-in-chief told reporters as he left the White House for a trip to the Philippines and China. “Usually, what happens with that is that any woman coming to the country that’s a beautiful woman that comes from China, they say she’s a spy.”
Trump also said that the national security of the country “was not put at risk” and that he “would not mind” if Huang was reinstated as Nvidia’s CEO.
Nvidia’s Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress has been named as interim CEO , and the chipmaking giant has hired an outside firm to seek a permanent replacement.
With Huang, one of the driving forces of the AI boom, missing in action, investors have been panicking that Nvidia’s dealmaking could slow — a potentially massive monkey wrench for the sector after recent weeks have seen Wall Street get jittery about the tech trade.

articles.title_orig: Warren Buffett donates more Berkshire shares, confidence 'as strong as ever'
articles.title_zh: Warren Buffett donates more Berkshire shares, confidence 'as strong as ever'
articles.content_orig:
Billionaire Warren Buffett donated Berkshire Hathaway shares worth about $5.5 billion to four philanthropic foundations, stepping up his annual charitable giving from the prior year.
Buffett, 96, converted 6,150 Class A Berkshire shares into 9,225,000 Class B shares and gave 3,690,000 of those shares to The Susan Thompson Buffett Foundation, and 1,845,000 shares each to The Sherwood Foundation, The Howard G. Buffett Foundation and NoVo Foundation — the foundations run by his three children, Susie, Howard and Peter Buffett.
Following the donations, the chairman emeritus of Berkshire still owns 182,140 Class A shares — roughly $162 billion.
"Last Thanksgiving I wrote that kindness is costless but also priceless. A year later, I would only add that it compounds, and at a better rate than anything Charlie and I ever bought," wrote Buffett, who was succeeded as chairman in September by his son Howard, in his annual Thanksgiving message.
The letter was much shorter than his message last Thanksgiving. Charlie Munger, former vice chairman of Berkshire, passed away in November 2023.
Berkshire shares have been on a tear recently, up more than 19% since the start of the fourth quarter and ending last week with four consecutive record high closes. That compares with the S&P 500's decline of 1.2% so far for the fourth quarter. Berkshire has been seen as a safe haven as investors have worried about the artificial intelligence buildout, corporate drama and geopolitical risk.
The shares are now outperforming the S&P 500 for the year by about 7.5 percentage points.
In his letter, Buffett reiterated that all of his Berkshire shares eventually will be donated to the four foundations, with the goal being to increase the size of the grants each year.
Buffett wrote that the gifts were a signal of his confidence not only in his three children, but also in Berkshire CEO Greg Abel:
"My children have given thoughtfully to worthy causes for decades, and I trust 100% both their abilities and their fidelity. ... You heard plenty from me in September about my confidence in Berkshire. That confidence is as strong as ever," he said.
Referring to Munger and himself, Buffett added, "Both of us received beyond measurement costless benefits from a few teachers such as Ben Graham, Joe Rosenfield and Tom Murphy. Because of this we not only prospered mightily but were able to pass along many of the benefits we received."
"Warren continues to share his wisdom with us all during this holiday season. His example reflects the kindness he encourages in all of us," said CEO Abel of the letter.
Buffett closes his message with this advice: "This Thanksgiving, thank one of those selfless people in your own life. Better yet, be a benefactor for someone else."

articles.title_orig: Cantwell calls out U.S. Secretary of Commerce for allowing China access to advanced AI technology
articles.title_zh: Cantwell calls out U.S. Secretary of Commerce for allowing China access to advanced AI technology
articles.content_orig:
Sen. Maria Cantwell , the top Democrat on the Senate commerce committee, alleged in a letter to Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick on Sunday that the department under his leadership failed to prevent China from accessing the U.S.'s most advanced artificial intelligence chips.
In the letter, Cantwell prodded Lutnick to enforce export controls and stop the flow of AI chips to companies barred from receiving the technology. She sent the missive ahead of a planned meeting this week between U.S. officials and Chinese President Xi Jinping on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation, in China.
Her urging comes as Washington reels from revelations that former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang had a relationship with an alleged Chinese spy named Alice Huang. Nvidia is the leading U.S. company designing advanced AI chips.
Alice Huang was an executive at Singaporean technology company Megaspeed that allegedly smuggled restricted chips to China.
Lutnick, meanwhile, has come under fire for stalling efforts to crack down on chip sales to China and for his close personal relationship with Jensen Huang, who was a vocal opponent of export controls.
"The Department of Commerce has resisted efforts to restrict companies flagged as national security threats, weakened safeguards, and left open pathways for the PRC to train advanced AI models using sensitive American technology," Cantwell wrote to Lutnick. "These failures to carry out the law help give away America's technology advantage in AI."
The Commerce Department did not immediately respond to a request for comment on Monday.
Cantwell called on Lutnick to use his authority to enforce a 2018 law, known as the Export Control Reform Act , which gives the Commerce Department broad latitude to enforce export controls and protect sensitive American technology.
She also cites potential financial conflicts involving Lutnick's sons , who control Cantor Fitzgerald, which she said held $1.2 billion in Nvidia stock at the time of his nomination. And she notes the Trump administration's 25% fee on certain Nvidia chips sold to China, which she said could create "a perverse financial incentive to approve exports of sensitive American technology."
"America's national security and AI leadership cannot be compromised by family business interests or a policy that generates federal revenue from exporting technology critical to our competitive edge," Cantwell wrote.
Both Democratic and Republican members of Congress have ramped up pressure on Lutnick and other Commerce Department officials after a Nov. 9 New York Times report alleging the department may have slow-walked an investigation into Megaspeed.
On Thursday, Senate banking committee Chair Tim Scott , R-S.C., summoned both Huang and Lutnick t o testify before his committee in December.
Lutnick has agreed to appear before the panel, Kristen Eichamer, a Commerce Department spokesperson, said in a statement last week.
And Democrats, who will take control of both the House and Senate in January, have signaled they will investigate Jensen Huang and Commerce officials.
On Wednesday, Sen. Elizabeth Warren , D-Mass., the top Democrat on the Senate banking panel, and Sen. Chris Coons , D-Del., the top Democrat on the Senate Foreign Relations subpanel with jurisdiction over East Asia and the Pacific, sent a letter to Lutnick, Secretary of State Marco Rubio and White House Chief of Staff Stephen Miller instructing them to preserve all documents and communications related to Nvidia's exports of "advanced AI chips to China or to entities that may divert such chips to China."
The letter gives all three officials until Nov. 17 to confirm that preservation directives have been issued.

articles.title_orig: A Bull Market for Pokémon Cards, Fueled by Pikachu and Nostalgia
articles.title_zh: A Bull Market for Pokémon Cards, Fueled by Pikachu and Nostalgia
articles.content_orig:
Scott Pratte turned his boyhood hobby into his livelihood. But he doesn’t usually tell people he’s a Pokémon card collector.
In conversations, he is vague about what he does for a living, saying his business involves collectibles or investments.
“I wouldn’t want to share numbers on the record,” Mr. Pratte, 39, said in an interview, though he noted that the past few years have been “million-dollar years in earnings.”
Pokémon originated as a pair of video games released in Japan for Nintendo’s Game Boy console in 1996. The franchise expanded to include a trading card game, released the same year, which came to the United States in 1999. That’s when Mr. Pratte and others first marveled at the artwork, swapped cards on playgrounds and obsessed over completing sets they shrouded in plastic sleeves in protective binders.
As Pokémon has grown — on its 30th anniversary, the franchise now spans TV shows and films, all manner of merchandise and a stable of more than 1,000 “pocket monsters” — the cards have skyrocketed in value.

articles.title_orig: Serena Williams winds down her VC firm, launches new fund, targets $200M
articles.title_zh: Serena Williams winds down her VC firm, launches new fund, targets $200M
articles.content_orig:
Serena Williams and longtime business partner Beth Ferreira announced Monday the launch of an early-stage firm called Starfire Ventures.
The firm is seeking to raise $200 million in capital to back AI-native companies that are “solving critical, underserved problems for individuals across the experience economy,” including in areas such as fintech and health and wellness, the fund said in a press release announcing its launch .
This fund is separate from Serena Ventures, which Williams founded in 2022. A rep for Starfire confirmed that Serena Ventures has recently cut its last check, though a team remains to support the existing portfolio. Serena Ventures backed more than 100 companies and raised over $100 million in capital. Ferreira worked as an advisor and general partner at Serena Ventures and has co-invested with Williams since 2015 when they backed MasterClass’ seed round.
This new firm, Starfire, is a continuation of that business partnership, with Williams saying in the press release that it was “designed to live beyond” them and that the goal remains to broaden “access to capital” and create “opportunities for more people to participate in the ownership and growth of transformative businesses.”

articles.title_orig: 7 Things We Just Learned About the Next-Gen Xbox
articles.title_zh: 7 Things We Just Learned About the Next-Gen Xbox
articles.content_orig:
As part of Xbox's 25th anniversary celebrations today, we've been treated to a new digital version of a magazine that was given out at Seattle FanFest earlier this week, available to read in full over on the official Xbox Wire website .
The bit that's getting most attention concerns Xbox Project Helix - the new next-gen console that's currently in the works over at Xbox HQ. The brand's VP of Next Generation, Jason Ronald, shares tons of new information across four pages in the magazine, helping to give us a better idea of what to expect from the upcoming console.
There's one section in particular that's getting all the interest on social media right now, where he clarifies that Project Helix is definitely a console that can play PC games, and definitely not a PC that happens to play console games.
"We're very clear on the design goal: Helix is designed to be a console that is also capable of playing games from your PC. It is not a PC that can also play console games. The goal is making it easy, intuitive, and instant to access my games. But if you're a hardcore gamer or a power user who wants to have that deeper level of customizability across settings and performance options, you can absolutely go do it."
Beyond this, Ronald talks in depth about loads of other aspects of what they're aiming for with Project Helix, and as mentioned, there's so much detail that it spreads across four pages of the magazine.
In the interest of highlighting as much as possible though, we thought we'd transcribe all of most notable quotes from the magazine down below, whereas you can read the added context inside of the magazine article itself.
Here are more of the key bits from the magazine article:
"When we think about Project Helix, it's really designed to be the ultimate gaming machine - one that removes all barriers of play that have historically existed. My entire library is accessible to me. I'm able to bring four generations of my Xbox library and progression with me and have it available instantly. And we remove the arbitrary constraints between console and PC games."
"We don't think the next generation is defined by 8K or 240 hertz, or some of the traditional metrics - it's really about gameplay innovation. It's about deeper immersion. It is about leveraging new technical advancements such as neural rendering, to deliver a new level of visual fidelity in more efficient and innovative ways. It's about new kinds of games and new game experiences that we haven't been able to do before. What excites me about the future is the idea of entirely new types of games that have never been possible before, delivered through all the innovation in the silicon and the hardware and the platform that we're delivering."
"When I think about what makes a console magical, it's that it just makes my games instantly accessible and ready to play in an instant. I don't have to worry about updating my operating system, updating drivers, configuring different settings - things like that. The hardware and the experience is entirely designed around playing games."
"The very first next-generation conversations we had were with all of our first-party studios. That was absolutely foundational to the design of what we've done with Project Helix - talking about where they saw the future of game design going, where they saw the future of their franchises going, and what was constraining their creative ambition."
"With Xbox One, I think we got so focused on expanding our aperture that we lost sight of what truly is magical, which is players, developers, and the games that they love. We have to build the best platform for game developers to deliver their creative vision."
"The other thing, and I think this is something that is unique about Xbox, is we have to be connected to the community. A lot of the features that people have come to love and expect from Xbox have actually been driven directly by community feedback. I think that's really core to the soul of who Xbox is, because if you're in touch with your player base, you never go wrong if you focus on what their needs are."
"It's definitely a challenging time, but as a system and a platform designer, it's also one of the most exciting times, because we have to invent entirely new technology to continue to advance the state-of-the-art while also continuing to make things accessible and affordable."
"This is a big reason why we're really focused on advancements like neural rendering, because it's an entirely new way to generate a frame without requiring more computational horsepower, additional memory, and things like that. I think you're going to see more innovation over the next three to five years than you've seen in the last 10 years."
"The ROG Xbox Ally was really an opportunity for us to learn alongside our player base with a lot of these concepts and the ideas that we had: being able to play libraries from across multiple different storefronts, understanding how PC games and console games can show up together in a unified library. The feedback that we've gotten from players has fundamentally informed and altered our plans of how it actually shows up in a future console. Players shared where we met the mark and areas we needed to improve or approach differently. So absolutely, we view the Ally as a precursor to what we're doing with Helix - but it's informed by a lot of the design concepts we have for Helix."
Sorry for the wall of quotes, but we thought you might find all of this pretty interesting! It's not even the full extent of what Ronald had to say, as he also touched on the importance of game preservation to the Xbox platform in general, as well as how Project Helix will seemingly have a bespoke UI, but one that still feels familiar to Xbox fans.
Of course, we're still waiting on concrete details about what Helix will look like, how much it'll cost, how significant the PC integration will be, and loads of other things that will give us a much better picture of how it'll shape up.
It seems like we won't be getting that this year though, and if rumours are to be believed, Xbox might even be releasing a first-party handheld in 2027 before the Project Helix console in 2028 . Who knows... plans can always change.
For now, let us know what you think about this latest info on Xbox Project Helix down below, and we definitely recommend reading the full Xbox 25th anniversary magazine for yourself - we wish we could buy one to be honest!

articles.content_orig:

The rapid proliferation of hyperscale data centres (HDCs) in the USA—mainly driven by the adoption of artificial intelligence—has raised concerns about this industry’s carbon footprint. We compiled facility-level information on 403 US hyperscale data centres operating between May 2024 and April 2025 and estimated their electricity consumption, electricity sources and attributable CO 2 emissions. Across facility-load scenarios, these HDCs consumed approximately 68–99 TWh of electricity and were associated with approximately 21–31 million metric tons of CO 2 under a location-based, total-output balancing-authority attribution method. Under the central scenario, HDC electricity demand was approximately 82 TWh, corresponding to about 1.8% of total US electricity consumption, and attributable CO 2 emissions were approximately 25.7 Mt. Roughly 54% of attributed generation was supplied by fossil-fuel sources. The HDC electricity-weighted total-output carbon intensity was approximately 314 gCO 2 kWh −1 , compared with a US total-output average of approximately 348 gCO 2 kWh −1 . Our approach provides a facility-resolved attributional framework for assessing the carbon footprint of hyperscale data centres using plant-level electricity-generation and emissions data.

Requests may be directed to the corresponding author. We provide public state- and balancing-authority-level data exports containing the electricity demand, attributable CO 2 emissions, total-output carbon intensity and attributed fuel mix used in the revised analysis. These aggregate exports reflect the central facility-load scenario ( u = 0.58) and the total-output attribution basis used for the headline results. They are available through the public reproducibility repository 46 . The repository exports, rather than the separate visualization interface, constitute the authoritative public data products for the revised analysis. Because the underlying facility data are protected by a data-use agreement, raw facility identifiers, addresses, coordinates and commercially sensitive facility attributes are not publicly released. The complete facility-level map-generation workflow requires authorized access to those inputs. Access to facility-level map coordinates remains subject to provider authorization and the data-use agreement; public aggregate files do not substitute for the restricted facility-level observations. Source data are provided with this paper.
All code used to estimate HDC power capacity, evaluate the capacity model, compute electricity use and emissions, validate public aggregate exports and reproduce manuscript-facing numerical results is publicly available in the public reproducibility repository 46 . A tagged snapshot corresponding to the Round 3 reproducibility materials is available as version v0.3.1-round3-final 47 . The repository contains: (1) the fully specified scikit-learn capacity-model pipeline, including disclosed predictors, preprocessing, effective hyperparameters, software version and evaluation metrics; (2) a non-identifying 403-row synthetic facility fixture with six missing power-capacity values; (3) a deterministic public synthetic split artefact at results/tables/synthetic_validation/splits.json , together with random and grouped validation outputs; (4) REPRO.md , documenting the validation sample, explicit imputation indicator, software versions, restricted-data workflow and emissions-accounting conventions; (5) scripts/reproduce_model.py , which regenerates the public synthetic validation outputs and writes the deterministic split artefact; (vi) the total-output emissions-attribution workflow using EPA eGRID2023 Revision 2; (7) denominator-audit, plant-inventory, public-export, restricted-data and manuscript-output validation scripts and (8) aggregate state- and balancing-authority-level exports used to verify the headline results. The public synthetic and aggregate materials allow external researchers to execute the capacity-model validation workflow, verify the emissions denominator, reproduce headline scenario totals, sum the public regional exports and run the repository tests without access to restricted facility records.

articles.title_orig: Intel stock falls after investors file class action lawsuit against the company
articles.title_zh: Intel stock falls after investors file class action lawsuit against the company
articles.content_orig:
Oops, something went wrong
Intel ( INTC ) stock fell more than 6% Monday morning as the market reacted to news that the company is facing a class action lawsuit from investors.
In the lawsuit filed on Friday , Intel shareholders claim the technology company misled investors about the impact of a slowdown in PC sales on its revenue. The complaint also claims Intel hid that supply limits blocked the company from meeting data center demand.
When those realities came to light in Intel's third quarter earnings report last month, shares dropped 28.6% the next day, losing around $140 billion of market value in the company's largest single-day decline in more than 50 years
"Any positive impacts to Intel's business and financial results resulting from data center construction and other aspects of the AI boom were more than offset by the negative effects on the Company's business and financial results resulting from the PC market slowdown and the excess inventory buildup described," read the lawsuit filed by Robbins Geller Rudman & Dowd.
The complaint states that in January, CEO Lip-Bu Tan claimed Intel was prepared to capture "unprecedented demand" for its products as a result of AI-related infrastructure projects. In July, Intel executive vice president and CFO David Zinsner also said a PC slowdown would allow Intel to shift production toward data center CPUs.
However, on the October call, Zinsner said the company was also facing severe supply constraints, including a shortage of substrates, a key material used in packaging chips, which undercut that story.
The l awsuit seeks to represent those who invested in Intel between July 23 and Oct. 29 of this year.
Intel stock is down nearly 50% over the past six months, following a substantial climb earlier in the year.

articles.title_orig: Bahrain court sentences dozens of Shia Muslims to life in prison, activists say
articles.title_zh: Bahrain court sentences dozens of Shia Muslims to life in prison, activists say
articles.content_orig:
Sixty-four Shia Muslims, most of them clerics, have been sentenced to life in prison in Bahrain on Iran-linked terrorism charges, according to a UK-based human rights group.
The Bahrain Institute for Rights and Democracy (BIRD) said another five people were handed 15-year prison sentences by the High Criminal Court in Manama.
The advocate general confirmed the sentences but did not give the number of defendants or identify them. He said they were accused of establishing a terrorist group linked to Iran's Revolutionary Guards.
BIRD condemned the verdicts, saying there had been "credible allegations of torture, coerced confessions, and severe restrictions on the defence".
Authorities in the Sunni Muslim-ruled kingdom have reportedly detained hundreds of people, most of them members of its Shia majority, on suspicion of espionage and terrorism offences since the start of the US and Israel's war with regional Shia power Iran in February.
Dozens have also been stripped of their Bahraini citizenship after being accused by the government of "sympathy and praise for Iran's hostile and criminal acts".
Iran has launched thousands of missiles and drones at Bahrain and other Gulf Arab states hosting US forces during the war. On Sunday, the Bahraini military said it had intercepted "several Iranian aerial attacks".
Fifty-six of the defendants sentenced on Monday were arrested in May and June.
BIRD said 47 of them were Shia clerics - including Sheikh Mohammed Sanqour and Sheikh Ali al-Sadadi, who led Friday prayers at the Imam al-Sadiq Grand Mosque in Duraz, and Sayed Moosa al-Alwedaie, who served as imam at the Grand Mosque in Ras Rumman - and nine were their affiliates, including religious reciters.
The 13 other defendants - including the exiled cleric Sheikh Isa Qassim, who holds the religious rank of ayatollah and ​is widely regarded as the spiritual ​leader of Bahrain's Shia community - were tried in absentia, it said. Bahraini authorities said most of them were in Iran.
The 64 defendants faced charges including establishing a terrorist group, which the Public Prosecution said was linked to Iran's Islamic Revolution Guard Corps (IRGC), and calling for the suspension of the provisions of the constitution and a change in the system of government.
The prosecution alleged that they had incited terrorist acts and promoted "Velayat-e Faqih" (rule by the supreme jurist), which is the backbone of Iran's theocratic system.
The High Criminal Court convicted all the defendants and imposed prison sentences ranging from 15 years to life, the advocate general and head of the Terrorist Crimes Prosecution announced . The court also fined some of the defendants $265,000 (£200,000) and ordered the confiscation of $21.2m (£16m) for charitable purposes.
The director of BIRD, Sayed Ahmed Alwadaei, said the verdicts were "deeply unjust" and constituted "an attack on the faith and identity of Bahrain's Shia community".
Reuters news agency cited a person close to the clerics' defence teams as describing the sentences as "worse than anything we imagined".
Last week, BIRD, Human Rights Watch and Amnesty International were among 20 human rights groups which signed an open letter calling on Bahraini authorities to investigate what they described as "serious allegations of torture" in the case.
They said defendants had reported being "subjected to forced standing, prolonged blindfolding and handcuffing, sleep deprivation, and threats of physical and sexual violence against themselves and their families, as well as citizenship revocation and deportation". Many were pressured to sign lengthy statements they were not allowed to read, they added.
The advocate general insisted on Monday that all the defendants' legal rights had been guaranteed during the investigation and that they had been given a fair trial.

articles.title_orig: Someone rebuilt old Android versions in your browser, and it's an instant nostalgia hit [Gallery]
articles.title_zh: Someone rebuilt old Android versions in your browser, and it's an instant nostalgia hit [Gallery]
articles.content_orig:
The “Android Time Machine” is a fun project that puts Android versions into your browser, giving you a quick and easy chance to play around with older versions for a quick hit of nostalgia.
Built on the back of AOSP builds for classic Nexus devices, “Android Time Machine” lets you quickly  access older Android versions. Specifically, Android 2.1 Eclair through Android 7.1.2 Nougat.
The simulator runs within the shell of a matching Nexus smartphone on a desktop browser, or to fit your actual smartphone if you run it on Android.
Versions and simulated smartphones include :
The best part here is how it works on your actual smartphone. When launched in fullscreen, it  scales to match your phone’s screen – meaning it fits even devices like the Galaxy Z Fold 8’s smaller outer display (it just shows the desktop version when open).
Since this is running through the browser and not an actual Android build, you won’t get a perfect replication. Performance is a little hit or miss, especially with certain animations, but it works really well overall.
The browser even simulates results from each era (oh, to go back to when Google Search wasn’t an absolute mess ). Similarly, Google apps and the camera are filled with placeholders since the web app can’t access the actual camera or connect to the internet to sign into a Google account.
Seeing things like the boot animations and live wallpapers from classic Nexus phones, as well as peeking back at lost apps like Google+ and Play Music, is just such a fun little piece of nostalgia.
“Android Time Machine” is free, and the source code is available on GitHub .

articles.title_orig: Airstrikes on Iran Missile Sites May Shed Light on Justification for Dams
articles.title_zh: Airstrikes on Iran Missile Sites May Shed Light on Justification for Dams
articles.content_orig:
Environmentalists have long been mystified by the significant proliferation of dams and water transfer projects like pipelines and tunnels across Iran, especially in regions that had no apparent need for them.
Some analysts think they now know the answer after U.S. and Israeli airstrikes on concealed Iranian missile sites this year targeted many of the same areas. These analysts have concluded that the water projects may have been developed to support the country’s military buildup.
Given the secrecy surrounding Iran’s missile program, any connection between it and Iran’s ambitious, decades-old initiative to develop water infrastructure remains speculative. But some experts find the evidence highly suggestive.
Nima Shokri, an expert on water security, and his team at the Hamburg University of Technology, in Germany, had for years tracked an unusually high number of dams across Iran — at least 533 of them, among the most of any country in the region.
“It was always puzzling to me,” he said. “Why were they building so many dams?”
In the spring, Dr. Shokri was perusing news about the war in his home country when he came across a map plotting airstrikes that had targeted suspected military sites. The pattern — a semicircle of dots from north to south — nearly matched that of his own map marking the locations of dams.
His old question, he said, was superseded by a new one: “Why does it seem that wherever we have dams, there is a missile strike close by?”

articles.title_zh: Trump Says He’s Open to Reinstatement of Jensen Huang as Nvidia Chief
articles.content_orig:
President Trump said on Monday that he was open to seeing Jensen Huang reinstated as the head of Nvidia, his latest public expression of support for the tech executive who resigned after admitting to an affair with a woman whom U.S. officials had identified as a Chinese intelligence asset.
“I would not mind; I would not mind that,” Mr. Trump told reporters on the South Lawn of the White House as he departed for a trip to Asia, including a stop in China.
“I think he learned a big lesson — I guess maybe one lesson is more important than another,” he added.
The president cast doubt on whether Alice Huang , the woman with whom Mr. Huang had a relationship, was actually a spy.
“I don’t know that she is a spy,” Mr. Trump said. “Usually, what happens with that is that any woman coming to the country that’s a beautiful woman that comes from China, they say she’s a spy. I don’t know that she was a spy at all.”

articles.title_orig: Chip stocks fall on US semiconductor restrictions: AlphaCheck
articles.title_zh: Chip stocks fall on US semiconductor restrictions: AlphaCheck
articles.content_orig:
Shares of Micron ( MU -6.49% ) stumbled out of the gate Friday morning, falling as much as 7.8%. As of 12:13 p.m. ET, the stock was still down 5.9%.
The catalyst that sent the semiconductor specialist lower was reports of the latest U.S. government efforts to prevent advanced artificial intelligence (AI) chips from reaching China.
Image source: Getty Images.
The U.S. Department of Commerce, in collaboration with the Department of Treasury and the National Security Council, issued a new "interim final rule," aimed at curbing the flow of AI chips and computing power to China. The rule would apply to companies with locations in certain high-risk countries, including China, Russia, and Iran, according to a report in The New York Times.
Moreover, these companies -- particularly those with locations in Indonesia, Malaysia, Thailand, Singapore, and Brazil -- would be required to vet their customers and apply for export licenses, according to the report. There are allegations that by gaining remote access to data centers in neighboring countries, China has been able to sidestep U.S. export controls.
On another front, the U.S. and its allies, including Japan, Israel, Australia, and the United Kingdom (U.K.), are compiling a list of critical AI components and technologies that require additional monitoring to prevent their export to China, according to a report in the Financial Times.
NASDAQ · As of 2:12 PM ET 11/16/26
This all comes at a critical juncture for AI investors. The resignation of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang set off a firestorm of criticism that more could have been done to prevent the smuggling of these technologies into China.
Micron is one of several companies at the cutting edge of memory chips used to facilitate AI processing and, as such, has experienced blistering sales and profit growth in recent years. Any measures taken by the U.S. government to restrict the sale of chips to China's neighbors will reduce overall demand.
This only adds to existing investor concerns about the durability of AI demand and where it goes from here. These fears have driven Micron down roughly 40% from its recent high (as of this writing), and the stock now sells for less than 10 times earnings. This presents investors with a compelling opportunity to buy Micron at a discount.

articles.title_orig: The Children's Place plans store closures after filing for bankruptcy, sets gift card deadline
articles.title_zh: The Children's Place plans store closures after filing for bankruptcy, sets gift card deadline
articles.content_orig:
California shoppers could lose some of their local The Children's Place stores as the struggling children's clothing retailer seeks bankruptcy protection and searches for a buyer to keep the nearly 60-year-old chain in business.
The retailer has 48 locations in California. Although the company says some closures are unavoidable, it has not identified which locations will close.
In New Jersey, where The Children's Place is headquartered in Secaucus, the outlook is more definitive. The retailer plans to close all 24 of its New Jersey stores, including Gymboree locations, by Feb. 4, 2027, according to a state-required layoff notice filed Nov. 6. The closures will put approximately 732 employees out of work, Patch reported . The fate of more than 500 stores in 43 other states remains uncertain.
The Children's Place and its sister brand, Gymboree, remain open for business, but the bankruptcy filing has brought deep discounts and some important changes for customers. All purchases made after Nov. 6 are final sales, and customers have a limited window to use gift cards and rewards points.
The retailer announced Sunday it has filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in U.S. Bankruptcy Court in New Jersey, seeking to sell substantially all its assets while continuing operations.
The company is negotiating with multiple potential buyers and hopes to find one willing to keep the business operating. Bids are due Dec. 9, and the company expects to complete the court-supervised sale process by the end of December.
In the meantime, the future of hundreds of stores across North America hangs in the balance.
The Children's Place is clear about the need to shrink its footprint. The company currently operates the following stores in California:
"Unfortunately, we have determined that certain store closures will be necessary during this process," the company said in a customer advisory .
The company said it is evaluating its locations and will announce closures as decisions are finalized. For now, all locations remain open and are offering discounts of up to 60 percent on all inventory. Those sales are intended to raise cash while the retailer looks for a buyer, but the company acknowledges that liquidation could become necessary if its rescue effort fails.
Although a full liquidation isn't the desired outcome, the company said it must plan for the contingency that an operational sale may fail to materialize .
The bankruptcy filing comes just as many California families are shopping for holiday outfits, children's winter clothing and Christmas gifts. There are bargains to be had, but also some catches.
Here's what shoppers should know:
Returns and exchanges: Purchases made after Nov. 6 are final and cannot be returned or exchanged. Eligible purchases made between Oct. 23 and Nov. 6 may still qualify for returns or exchanges under the existing policy, subject to court approval.
Gift cards: The Children's Place and Gymboree gift cards will continue to be accepted for a limited period, subject to court approval. The company has not announced a final redemption date. Once that deadline passes, remaining balances will not be redeemable for cash.
Rewards points: Customers can continue redeeming My Place Rewards points temporarily, subject to court approval. The program will eventually be discontinued, and unused points will expire.
Online orders: The retailer expects online orders and deliveries to continue without interruption.
Discounts: Inventory sales are underway both online and in stores, with substantial markdowns.
The company is encouraging shoppers to use gift cards and rewards points while they are still valid rather than risk losing their value.
The Children's Place has been dressing generations of American children for nearly six decades, building its business around affordable clothing for babies, toddlers and older kids.
But the company has struggled with declining sales, rising costs and competition in a retail market where shoppers have plenty of alternatives.
The bankruptcy filing gives the retailer an opportunity to reorganize its finances while seeking a buyer willing to preserve the business.
"Today's announcement marks an important step in our efforts to secure the best path forward for The Children's Place," Rudy Morando, the company's co-chief restructuring officer, said in the announcement.
The company is seeking financing to keep operating during the bankruptcy proceedings, and it has asked the court for permission to continue paying employees and suppliers.

TEHRAN, Nov. 16 (MNA) – Bahrain's highest religious authority Grand Ayatollah Sheikh Isa Qassim has been sentenced to life imprisonment in Bahrain on Monday.
Bahrain’s High Criminal Court issued a life sentence on Monday, in absentia, against Ayatollah Sheikh Isa Qassim, a prominent Bahraini cleric.
The court session took place following a 40-day conflict, amidst a wave of widespread arrests of religious scholars and activists, as well as the revocation of the citizenship of hundreds of individuals.
Four other clerics have also been sentenced to 15 years in prison.
Prior to this, the Bahraini opposition had dismissed the trial of several prominent Shia clerics, holding the government responsible for the consequences of any convictions that might be handed down against the detained clerics. These groups warned that continuation of such actions would push political crisis into a phase of confrontation that threatens the very existence of one of the core components of Bahraini society.
Opposition forces have called on the people of Bahrain to follow developments and to remain prepared to defend the religious scholars and Shia community, in accordance with the guidance of Ayatollah Sheikh Isa Ahmed Qassim, who has emphasized the importance of remaining loyal to the scholars.

Houthi fighters have advanced to within 100 km of Aden, the temporary capital of Yemen’s Saudi-backed government, after government forces withdrew from positions near the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, Yemeni military sources said on Monday. Tankers carrying Saudi crude from the Red Sea port of Yanbu to buyers in Asia pass through the strait .
Brent crude futures fell 2.32% to $93.62 a barrel at 9:43 a.m. ET, and West Texas Intermediate (WTI) dropped 1.93% to 86.85. Murban, Abu Dhabi’s benchmark crude, rose 1.52% to 94.89.
Five Yemeni military sources told Reuters that Houthi fighters had reached Khor Omairh, about 100 km west of Aden. The government had said on Sunday it was pulling out of Dhubab and the surrounding area near the strait to defend the city. Maritime Executive reported on Nov. 3 that Houthi control of the coast between Bab el-Mandeb and Aden “would present a major increase in the threat posed to merchant shipping” using the strait and the Maritime Security Transit Corridor through the Gulf of Aden.
Houthi spokesman Yahya Saree said on Thursday that the group struck Pumping Station No. 7 on the East-West Pipeline and the Yanbu oil facility, The New Arab reported . The group has vowed to keep attacking Saudi Arabia under a principle of “siege for siege, airport for airport, and escalation for escalation,” Al Jazeera reported .
The Red Sea has been Saudi Arabia’s main oil export hub since the Iran war began in February, Reuters columnist Ron Bousso wrote on Monday. The East-West Pipeline can carry up to 7 million barrels per day from the kingdom’s eastern oilfields to Yanbu, according to The National . A drone attack in September that Riyadh blamed on a pro-Iranian militia in Iraq shut the line until Sept. 22.
Strategic affairs expert Ali al-Dahab told Al Jazeera that the Houthis aim their missile and drone campaign at Saudi Arabia, not at the authorities in Aden, and that the group’s gains along Bab el-Mandeb mean it “now directly and completely control[s] the western Yemeni coastal sector and part of the maritime extension towards Aden.”

articles.title_orig: 'iPhone 20 Pro' Rumored to Be Based on iPhone Air
articles.title_zh: 'iPhone 20 Pro' Rumored to Be Based on iPhone Air
articles.content_orig:
Next year's "iPhone 20 Pro" models will use the same glass design as the iPhone Air , but with more pronounced curvature along all four sides, according to the leaker known as " Fixed Focus Digital ."
In a new post on Weibo, the leaker said the device would use the same glass material as the ‌iPhone Air‌, adjusted to have greater curvature and produce a four-sided curved effect. The accompanying hashtag refers specifically to an "iPhone 20 Pro" with a four-sided curved, "all-glass" design.
An illustration shared with the post depicts rounded front and rear glass meeting a narrow, polished, gold-colored metallic frame. Physical side buttons, antenna lines, and a protruding rear camera assembly remain visible.
Taken together with earlier rumors and the post's accompanying illustration, the repeated comparisons suggest a design somewhere between the iPhone X and ‌iPhone Air‌. The ‌iPhone Air‌ provides a reference for the slim profile and a more modern iPhone design, while the more pronounced glass curvature recalls the rounded edges of the iPhone X. Both feature a polished frame.
The latest claim builds on Fixed Focus Digital's previous report that Apple had modified ‌iPhone Air‌ manufacturing equipment to produce more rounded glass components for the 20th anniversary models. The leaker said the changes had helped reduce manufacturing costs, while substantially improving thinness and heat dissipation.
In a still-earlier report , the same leaker also claimed that a supply chain facility had completed renovations ahead of "iPhone 20" production, with manufacturing quality expected to be roughly comparable to the first-generation ‌iPhone Air‌. The ‌iPhone Air‌ features Ceramic Shield 2 on the front and Ceramic Shield on the back.
The broader design picture aligns with Bloomberg 's Mark Gurman 's reporting that Apple's anniversary Pro models will feature glass that curves into the sides from both the front and rear, with a thin metal band between the two panels. Gurman has also described thinner display bezels and curved glass around all corners and edges, in what he expects to be the biggest overhaul of the Pro line since the iPhone X.
Apple's 20th-anniversary iPhone models are expected to launch in the fall of 2027 . While leakers have variably referred to the device as the "iPhone 20 Pro," Apple's naming plans remain unclear. It seems plausible that the company could skip the iPhone 19 name to emphasize the anniversary, similar to its introduction of the iPhone X in 2017.

articles.title_orig: Chip tensions loom over Trump-Xi summit, as US and China push AI safety steps
articles.title_zh: Chip tensions loom over Trump-Xi summit, as US and China push AI safety steps
articles.content_orig:
Sen. Maria Cantwell , the top Democrat on the Senate commerce committee, alleged in a letter to Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick on Sunday that the department under his leadership failed to prevent China from accessing the U.S.'s most advanced artificial intelligence chips.
In the letter, Cantwell prodded Lutnick to enforce export controls and stop the flow of AI chips to companies barred from receiving the technology. She sent the missive ahead of a planned meeting this week between U.S. officials and Chinese President Xi Jinping on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation, in China.
Her urging comes as Washington reels from revelations that former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang had a relationship with an alleged Chinese spy named Alice Huang. Nvidia is the leading U.S. company designing advanced AI chips.
Alice Huang was an executive at Singaporean technology company Megaspeed that allegedly smuggled restricted chips to China.
Lutnick, meanwhile, has come under fire for stalling efforts to crack down on chip sales to China and for his close personal relationship with Jensen Huang, who was a vocal opponent of export controls.
"The Department of Commerce has resisted efforts to restrict companies flagged as national security threats, weakened safeguards, and left open pathways for the PRC to train advanced AI models using sensitive American technology," Cantwell wrote to Lutnick. "These failures to carry out the law help give away America's technology advantage in AI."
The Commerce Department did not immediately respond to a request for comment on Monday.
Cantwell called on Lutnick to use his authority to enforce a 2018 law, known as the Export Control Reform Act , which gives the Commerce Department broad latitude to enforce export controls and protect sensitive American technology.
She also cites potential financial conflicts involving Lutnick's sons , who control Cantor Fitzgerald, which she said held $1.2 billion in Nvidia stock at the time of his nomination. And she notes the Trump administration's 25% fee on certain Nvidia chips sold to China, which she said could create "a perverse financial incentive to approve exports of sensitive American technology."
"America's national security and AI leadership cannot be compromised by family business interests or a policy that generates federal revenue from exporting technology critical to our competitive edge," Cantwell wrote.
Both Democratic and Republican members of Congress have ramped up pressure on Lutnick and other Commerce Department officials after a Nov. 9 New York Times report alleging the department may have slow-walked an investigation into Megaspeed.
On Thursday, Senate banking committee Chair Tim Scott , R-S.C., summoned both Huang and Lutnick t o testify before his committee in December.
Lutnick has agreed to appear before the panel, Kristen Eichamer, a Commerce Department spokesperson, said in a statement last week.
And Democrats, who will take control of both the House and Senate in January, have signaled they will investigate Jensen Huang and Commerce officials.
On Wednesday, Sen. Elizabeth Warren , D-Mass., the top Democrat on the Senate banking panel, and Sen. Chris Coons , D-Del., the top Democrat on the Senate Foreign Relations subpanel with jurisdiction over East Asia and the Pacific, sent a letter to Lutnick, Secretary of State Marco Rubio and White House Chief of Staff Stephen Miller instructing them to preserve all documents and communications related to Nvidia's exports of "advanced AI chips to China or to entities that may divert such chips to China."
The letter gives all three officials until Nov. 17 to confirm that preservation directives have been issued.
